correctness.rationale: For Rademacher \(z\), the coordinate estimator decomposes as \(D_i=H_{ii}+\sum_{j\ne i}H_{ij}z_iz_j\), so orthogonality of distinct Rademacher monomials gives the exact variance \(\sum_{j\ne i}H_{ij}^2\). Independent probe averaging divides that variance by \(m\), while AdaHessian's bias-corrected RMS weights sum to one. The two-dimensional extremum reduces to a one-variable rational function and has the unique maximizer \(p=\kappa/(\kappa+1)\).

originality.rationale: The variance structure of Hutchinson diagonal estimation is known in the matrix-estimation literature. The surviving new claim is its exact implication after AdaHessian's RMS momentum: off-diagonal estimator variance becomes a persistent mean-square preconditioner term, with an exact probe-count law and a sharp condition-number inflation formula. The inspected AdaHessian and diagonal-estimation sources do not state this optimizer-level consequence.
residual_risks: The underlying one-probe variance identity is classical; originality rests on the exact AdaHessian RMS consequence and sharp conditioning refinement.
A specialized implementation note may have observed the same RMS bias without appearing in the indexed literature.
The public AdaHessian implementation performs absolute-value spatial averaging for blocks larger than one, so the main theorem intentionally uses block size one.

value.rationale: AdaHessian's defining design uses a cheap stochastic Hessian diagonal and then an RMS momentum to stabilize it. The theorem shows exactly what that RMS stabilizes around in mean square on a fixed quadratic: not the Hessian diagonal, but a quantity inflated by off-diagonal curvature. The sharp condition-number formula quantifies how large this effect can be, while the \(1/m\) law identifies a direct, source-compatible mitigation through additional probes. This distinguishes temporal smoothing from estimator-variance removal and is a natural diagnostic for a second-order adaptive preconditioner.
